description: Python framework for AI-powered conversational bots with YAML config, HTTP/Telegram channels, per-user memory, and sub-agent orchestration using claude-agent-sdk

userStories.title: Initialize Python project structure with pyproject.toml
userStories.description: As a bot developer, I want a proper Python project skeleton so that dependencies are managed and the package is installable
acceptanceCriteria: pyproject.toml exists with project name claude-code-bot and Python >=3.11
Dependencies include: fastapi, uvicorn, aiogram, pydantic, pyyaml, claude-agent-sdk, structlog
Dev dependencies include: pytest, httpx, mypy, ruff
src/claude_code_bot/ package directory exists with __init__.py
src/claude_code_bot/__main__.py exists as entry point
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Create Pydantic config models and YAML loader
userStories.description: As a bot developer, I want to define my bot's persona, channels, and settings in a YAML file validated by Pydantic so that I can configure behavior without writing Python code
acceptanceCriteria: Pydantic models defined: BotConfig, PersonaConfig (name, system_prompt, tone, constraints, greeting, fallback_message), ChannelConfig (type: http|telegram, settings dict), MemoryConfig (backend, path), SubAgentConfig (import_path, description, timeout), ApiKeysConfig (anthropic_api_key, telegram_bot_token)
YAML file at configurable path (default config.yaml) is loaded and validated at startup
Missing required fields produce Pydantic ValidationError naming the field and expected type
Missing YAML file produces clear 'Config file not found: <path>' error
Environment variables override YAML values (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY overrides api_keys.anthropic_api_key, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN overrides api_keys.telegram_bot_token)
A config.example.yaml is provided with all fields documented
Typecheck passes

verificationCommands.command: python -c "from claude_code_bot.config import load_config; print('import ok')"

userStories.notes: Write unit tests for valid config, missing fields, missing file, and env var override

userStories.title: Create FastAPI app with health check endpoint
userStories.description: As a bot developer, I want a /health endpoint so that I can verify the bot is running and integrate with uptime monitors
acceptanceCriteria: GET /health returns HTTP 200 with JSON body {"status": "ok"}
The endpoint requires no authentication
FastAPI app starts on http://localhost:8000 by default (port configurable via YAML or env var)
Typecheck passes

verificationCommands.command: timeout 5 bash -c 'python -m claude_code_bot &>/dev/null & sleep 2 && curl -s http://localhost:8000/health && kill %1' 2>/dev/null || true

userStories.title: Add structured JSON startup logging
userStories.description: As a bot developer, I want structured JSON logs on startup so that I can confirm which channels and features are active
acceptanceCriteria: On successful boot, a JSON log line is emitted containing: loaded config path, active channels, persona name
Log output goes to stdout
Log level is configurable via YAML or env var (default: INFO)
structlog is configured with JSON renderer
Typecheck passes

verificationCommands.command: python -c "from claude_code_bot.logging import setup_logging; setup_logging(); print('ok')"

userStories.title: Implement per-user conversation memory store
userStories.description: As an end user, I want the bot to remember our previous conversation so that I don't have to repeat context
acceptanceCriteria: MemoryBackend abstract base class with methods: load(user_id) -> list[Message], save(user_id, messages), clear(user_id)
JsonFileMemoryBackend stores one JSON file per user_id in configurable directory (default: data/)
Memory directory is created automatically if it does not exist
Each message has role (user/assistant), content, and timestamp
Separate conversation history per user_id
History survives process restart (verified by test)
Typecheck passes

verificationCommands.command: python -c "from claude_code_bot.memory import JsonFileMemoryBackend; print('import ok')"

userStories.notes: Tests should verify persistence across save/load cycles

userStories.title: Implement memory graceful degradation
userStories.description: As an end user, I want the bot to still respond even if memory storage fails so that a disk error does not break the conversation
acceptanceCriteria: If writing to the memory store raises an I/O error, the bot still returns the LLM response to the user
Memory failure is logged as a structured JSON warning
If memory file is unreadable on next turn, bot starts a fresh conversation context (no crash)
Typecheck passes

verificationCommands.command: pytest tests/ -k 'memory and (fail or degrad or error)' -v

userStories.title: Implement conversation history truncation
userStories.description: As a bot developer, I want long conversations to be truncated before sending to the LLM so that context window limits are not exceeded
acceptanceCriteria: Before each LLM call, conversation history is truncated to fit within configurable max token budget (default: 80% of model context window)
Truncation removes oldest messages first, always preserving system prompt and most recent N messages
Structured JSON log line emitted when truncation occurs, stating how many messages were removed
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use character-based approximation or tiktoken for token counting

userStories.title: Integrate claude-agent-sdk for main agent with persona
userStories.description: As a bot developer, I want the bot to respond consistently with the configured persona so that end users get the intended experience
acceptanceCriteria: claude-agent-sdk is used to generate responses
persona.system_prompt from YAML is passed as system prompt on every request
persona.name is available for use in responses
persona.constraints list is appended to the system prompt as behavioral rules
SDK calls are wrapped behind a thin abstraction layer (AgentService class) to mitigate API changes
Typecheck passes

verificationCommands.command: python -c "from claude_code_bot.agent import AgentService; print('import ok')"

userStories.notes: Mock claude-agent-sdk in tests to avoid API costs

userStories.title: Implement LLM error retry and fallback
userStories.description: As an end user, I want to receive a friendly message when the LLM is unavailable so that I am not left with a cryptic error
acceptanceCriteria: If claude-agent-sdk call fails (timeout, 5xx, rate limit), framework retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff
After all retries fail, bot returns configurable fallback message (default: "I'm having trouble thinking right now. Try again in a moment.")
Fallback message is configurable via persona.fallback_message in YAML
Each failure is logged as structured JSON error with exception type and attempt number
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement POST /chat HTTP endpoint
userStories.description: As an HTTP end user, I want to send a message and receive a response so that I can converse with the bot
acceptanceCriteria: POST /chat accepts JSON body {"user_id": "string", "message": "string"}
Returns JSON {"response": "string"} with the bot's reply
Response is generated by claude-agent-sdk using persona's system_prompt
If message is empty string, bot returns persona-appropriate 'I didn't catch that' response
If user_id is not previously seen, a new conversation context is created automatically
Conversation history is loaded from memory and included in LLM call
Response and user message are saved to memory
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use httpx TestClient for integration tests with mocked LLM

userStories.title: Add optional HTTP API key authentication
userStories.description: As a bot developer, I want to optionally require an API key for the HTTP channel so that I can restrict access in non-local deployments
acceptanceCriteria: If channels[http].api_key is set in config, requests to /chat without matching X-API-Key header return HTTP 401 with {"error": "Unauthorized"}
If channels[http].api_key is not set, /chat is open (no auth required)
/health never requires authentication regardless of config
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement sub-agent base class and registry
userStories.description: As a bot developer, I want to register custom sub-agents with the framework so that the main agent can delegate specialized tasks
acceptanceCriteria: BaseSubAgent abstract class with: name: str, description: str, async def handle(self, context: dict) -> str
SubAgentRegistry class with register(agent), list() -> list of names/descriptions, get(name) -> agent
Sub-agents registerable via YAML config (import_path) or programmatically via registry.register(instance)
On startup, configured sub-agents are loaded and registered; import failures produce clear error naming the failing agent
Typecheck passes

verificationCommands.command: python -c "from claude_code_bot.agents import BaseSubAgent, SubAgentRegistry; print('import ok')"

userStories.title: Wire sub-agents as tools in main agent
userStories.description: As an end user, I want the bot to use specialized capabilities when needed so that I get accurate, task-specific results
acceptanceCriteria: Main agent's system prompt includes description of each registered sub-agent and when to use them
Each sub-agent is exposed as a tool via claude-agent-sdk tool use
Sub-agent handle() receives context dict with: user_id, channel, query, conversation_summary
Sub-agent's string result is returned to main agent for incorporation into final response
If sub-agent raises exception or times out (configurable, default 30s), main agent receives error message and responds gracefully
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Mock claude-agent-sdk tool use in tests

userStories.title: Implement Telegram channel adapter
userStories.description: As a Telegram end user, I want to message the bot and receive a reply so that I can chat with it on Telegram
acceptanceCriteria: When telegram is listed in channels config with valid bot_token, bot connects to Telegram on startup
Bot receives text DMs via aiogram and responds with persona's reply
Telegram chat.id is used as user_id for memory
Default connection mode is long-polling (no webhook setup required)
If Telegram bot token is invalid, startup fails with clear error: 'Invalid Telegram bot token'
Typecheck passes

verificationCommands.command: python -c "from claude_code_bot.channels.telegram import TelegramChannel; print('import ok')"

userStories.notes: Mock aiogram in tests; test Telegram adapter in isolation

userStories.title: Add Telegram /start greeting for new users
userStories.description: As a Telegram end user, I want to receive an introduction when I first message the bot so that I know what it does
acceptanceCriteria: On /start command, bot sends a greeting message
If persona.greeting is configured in YAML, that text is used; otherwise bot generates organic introduction via LLM
Greeting is sent only once per user (tracked via memory store)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement proactive messaging on Telegram
userStories.description: As a bot developer, I want the bot to send messages to users without a prior trigger so that it can deliver reminders, follow-ups, or notifications
acceptanceCriteria: Framework exposes internal API send_proactive_message(user_id, message) callable from sub-agents or scheduled tasks
Message is delivered to user's Telegram chat
If user has never interacted with bot (no chat_id on record), call raises UserNotReachableError and logs warning
Proactive messages are persisted in conversation memory as assistant messages
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Wire sub-agent proactive message callback
userStories.description: As a bot developer, I want a sub-agent to be able to trigger a proactive message so that background tasks can notify users of results
acceptanceCriteria: Sub-agent handle() context includes a send_proactive callback function
Calling send_proactive(user_id, message) from within a sub-agent delivers message via Telegram channel
If Telegram is not configured, the call is a no-op and logs a warning
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Create Dockerfile for the bot
userStories.description: As a bot developer, I want to build and run the bot via Docker so that deployment is reproducible and requires no local Python setup
acceptanceCriteria: docker build -t claude-code-bot . succeeds and produces a working image
Dockerfile uses Python 3.11+ base image, installs dependencies from pyproject.toml
Image runs the bot with python -m claude_code_bot as default command
Config file is mountable via volume (default path: /app/config.yaml)
Typecheck passes

verificationCommands.command: docker run --rm claude-code-bot python -c "import claude_code_bot; print('ok')"

userStories.title: Create docker-compose.yml and .env.example
userStories.description: As a bot developer, I want docker compose up to start the bot with all configuration so that I can deploy with one command
acceptanceCriteria: docker-compose.yml at project root defines single service 'bot' building from local Dockerfile
Environment variables for secrets (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN) read from .env file
Config YAML and data directory mounted as volumes for persistence
docker compose up starts the bot; docker compose down stops it cleanly
.env.example file documents all required and optional environment variables
Typecheck passes
